When running make, you can set values for several variables to modify
compilation, installation and meta-information paths. If you do, you need to
include them in *every* call to make.

Variables:

* CC to set the C compiler. gcc by default, or cc if gcc is not available.
* LDFLAGS for additional linker flags, empty by default.
* AR, ARFLAGS and OBJCOPY to set the archiver, its flags and objcopy. ARFLAGS
  is rcsD by default. If your ar does not support the D (deterministic) flag,
  use ARFLAGS=rcs.
* PREFIX, which is /usr/local by default.
* MANDIR, which is $(PREFIX)/share/man by default.
* INCLUDEDIR, which is $(PREFIX)/include by default.
* LIBDIR, which is $(PREFIX)/lib64 by default if the system C library is in a
  lib64 directory (like in Fedora), or $(PREFIX)/lib otherwise.
* PKGCONFIGDIR, which is $(LIBDIR)/pkgconfig by default, or
  $(PREFIX)/libdata/pkgconfig in FreeBSD.

Only needed in the installation step:

When cross-compiling, set CC, AR and OBJCOPY to the tools for the target

make CC=aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc AR=aarch64-linux-gnu-ar \
